seo.title: Claude Code vs HagiCode: Features and Comparison
seo.description: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal coding agent; HagiCode is a workbench that runs it. Compare install, plans, features and when each fits.

summary: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal, IDEs, a desktop app and the web, billed through a Claude plan or an API account. HagiCode is a desktop workbench that runs Claude Code as its executor and adds parallel sessions, proposals and AI commits around it.

content: Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent: it reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and works with Git, in the terminal, in VS Code and JetBrains, in a desktop app or on the web. HagiCode is a desktop and web workbench that runs the Claude Code CLI as its executor. It does not replace Claude Code, and it does not host or resell Claude models.

Claude Code already covers a lot on its own, including subagents, background agents, hooks, skills and CI use. If you work in one place at a time and are happy with its own surfaces, stay with Claude Code alone. HagiCode is for people who want written proposals before changes, one workspace across repositories, and one view of many sessions and several different Agent CLIs.

sections.title: Claude Code vs HagiCode at a glance

cells: What it is
Anthropic's agentic coding tool; one engine behind the CLI, IDE extensions, desktop app and web
Desktop and web workbench that runs Agent CLIs, Claude Code among them; not a model or an agent itself
Interface and platforms
Terminal CLI on macOS, Windows (native or WSL) and Linux; VS Code, JetBrains, desktop app and claude.ai/code
Desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux; Docker Compose container; Microsoft Store edition
Pricing and licensing
Needs a Pro ($20 per month), Max (from $100), Team or Enterprise plan, a Console account, or Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry; free claude.ai plan excluded (as of October 2026)
Desktop and Container editions are free; Store edition is free with an optional one-time TurboEngine purchase
Model and provider access
Claude models through your Anthropic plan or a third-party cloud provider
Hosts no models; uses whatever your Claude Code install is signed in to; optional OmniRoute model catalog
Parallel work
Subagents, plus background agents to run several sessions and watch them from one screen
Several sessions side by side, each an Agent with a visible status, across any Agent CLI
Spec and planning workflow
Plan mode, CLAUDE.md memory, skills and hooks; no proposal archive of its own
OpenSpec proposals: propose, validate, apply, archive; free editions allow 3 concurrent proposals
Git and commit handling
Stages changes, writes commit messages, creates branches and opens pull requests when asked
AI-composed commits, repository locked while committing, per-repo targeting with Monospecs
Setup effort
One native installer, Homebrew, WinGet or npm command, then browser sign-in
Needs Claude Code installed and signed in first, then HagiCode Desktop on top
Best for
Developers who want the agent in their terminal or editor, with CI and scheduled tasks
Spec-driven work, many parallel sessions, multi-repo projects, mixing several Agent CLIs

items.title: Many surfaces, one engine
content: The terminal CLI, the VS Code and JetBrains integrations, the desktop app and the web version all use the same Claude Code engine, so CLAUDE.md files, settings and MCP servers carry across them. Remote Control lets you continue a local session from a phone or browser, and `claude --teleport` pulls a web session into your terminal.

items.title: Install paths and sign-in
content: The recommended install is `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash` on macOS, Linux and WSL, or `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell. Homebrew (`brew install --cask claude-code`), WinGet (`winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode`) and npm (`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`) also work. Run `claude --version`, then `claude` and follow the browser sign-in; native installs auto-update.
The free claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code, so you need a paid plan, a Console account or a cloud provider.

items.title: Customisation that lives in the repo
content: CLAUDE.md sets standards for every session, and Claude Code can read an AGENTS.md instead. Skills package repeatable workflows, hooks run shell commands before or after its actions, and auto memory saves what it learns between sessions.

items.title: Parallelism, automation and an SDK
content: Subagents split a task across agents with a lead coordinating, and background agents run several full sessions you can watch from one screen. `claude -p` suits pipes and CI, GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD are documented, routines and `/loop` handle scheduled work, and the Agent SDK builds custom agents on the same tools.

sections.title: When to choose Claude Code, and when to choose HagiCode

items: you want the agent in your terminal, VS Code or JetBrains and one task at a time is enough;
you rely on CI, GitHub Actions, `claude -p` or scheduled routines;
its own subagents, background agents and desktop app already cover your parallel work;
you keep project rules in CLAUDE.md, skills and hooks and do not need a proposal workflow;
you want to start tasks from the web or your phone and continue them locally.
you want a written proposal, reviewed before Claude Code edits anything and archived afterwards;
a Claude Code change has to land in a backend and a frontend repository together, and you want one workspace that knows both;
you run many sessions and also use other Agent CLIs, and want one list for all of them;
you would rather have Claude Code's changes summarised into a commit message for you, with a browser editor open next to the chat;
you want Claude Code's questions and waiting subagents shown as part of the session.

blocks.title: Where HagiCode is not the right tool
content: Headless CI and scripted one-shot runs belong to `claude -p`, GitHub Actions or the Agent SDK, not a desktop workbench.
If you only want a terminal, or one quick question in an editor that already has the Claude Code extension, HagiCode is more than you need.

HagiCode needs Claude Code installed and signed in first, so setup is longer than using Claude Code alone. Teams that do not want a proposal discipline will find it overhead, free editions cap concurrent proposals at 3, and the embedded Code Server editor is not a full IDE replacement.
Surfaces that live on Anthropic's side, such as the web version, Remote Control, routines and the Slack integration, stay there; HagiCode drives the local CLI.

sections.title: Using Claude Code together with HagiCode

content: HagiCode sits on top of the CLI. It starts your installed Claude Code, so your Anthropic plan, sign-in and usage limits stay with you, and HagiCode adds the session, proposal and repository layers around it.
Nothing is locked in. Your repositories, CLAUDE.md, skills and settings stay where they are, and you can run `claude` on the same project whenever you like.

items: Install Claude Code with the native installer, Homebrew, WinGet or npm, and confirm it with `claude --version`.
Run `claude` once and sign in, so it is authenticated before HagiCode uses it.
Install HagiCode Desktop for Windows, macOS or Linux, or use the Docker Compose or Microsoft Store edition.
In HagiCode's Agent CLI settings, pick Claude Code as the executor; HagiCode looks for the `claude` command on your PATH.
Open a repository and start a session or an OpenSpec proposal; tool calls, questions and waiting work appear in the session.
To go back, close HagiCode and run `claude` in the same folder; nothing needs to be undone.

blocks.title: What works with Claude Code inside HagiCode
content: Claude Code gets the full set: parallel sessions, Agents management, OpenSpec proposals, AI commits, Code Server, Monospecs, Vault, interactive questions and the agent work panel. The last two are not available for most other Agent CLIs.
Claude Code features that need Anthropic's own surfaces, such as the desktop app and Remote Control, are not part of HagiCode.

sections.title: What HagiCode adds on top of any agent

items.title: Parallel sessions and Agents management
content: Each Claude Code session becomes an Agent with its own context and a status you can scan. That sits alongside Claude Code's own subagents and background agents: HagiCode adds one list for sessions across folders and across different Agent CLIs.

items.title: OpenSpec proposals
content: A task can begin as an OpenSpec proposal that you write, validate, apply and archive. Claude Code implements within it, and the proposal keeps the decision record that CLAUDE.md and chat history do not.

items.title: AI commit and Code Server
content: HagiCode drafts commit messages from the changes Claude Code made and locks the repository while committing. The embedded Code Server editor opens the touched files beside the conversation.

items.title: Monospecs and Vault
content: Monospecs lists the repositories in a multi-repo workspace so one Claude Code task sees all of them. Vault keeps reference code and notes across projects, complementing what auto memory keeps per project.

items.title: Model routing, tool-call view and usage
content: Claude Code's tool calls appear in the same typed shape as every other CLI, live and in history. OmniRoute can supply a model catalog per Agent CLI, and an optional TokenMonitor readout in the status bar shows today's tokens and cost.

items.title: Interactive questions: let Claude Code ask, then continue the same run
content: When Claude Code needs a decision, it can ask a structured question during the run. HagiCode shows it in the conversation, the session changes from executing to waiting for a reply, and your answer lets the same run continue. If the run has ended, for example after a restart, the answer goes in as a normal message in the same session.
bullets: Questions asked at the same time can be answered in one submission;
An unanswered question expires after 30 minutes and can still be answered with a follow-up message;
Enabled per CLI through the interactive-control setting.

items.title: Agent work panel: know why a run is still going
content: While a run is executing, Claude Code may be waiting on subagents or monitors. HagiCode lists that work with its status, so you can see what the run is waiting for instead of guessing. The list is kept in memory for the current run and is recovered if you refresh the page.
bullets: Subagents and monitors that the host waits on are listed with their status;
The list is not saved with the conversation history;
Background commands that the host does not wait for are not listed.

items: Claude Code is the agent: it reads, edits, runs and commits. HagiCode is the workbench around it.
Stay with Claude Code alone for single-task, editor, CI or scheduled work; add HagiCode for proposals, many parallel sessions and multi-repo changes.
Claude Code needs to be installed and signed in first, and you can go back to running `claude` directly at any time.

faq.question: How do I install Claude Code?
faq.answer: On macOS, Linux or WSL run `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`; in Windows PowerShell run `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex`. Homebrew (`brew install --cask claude-code`), WinGet (`winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode`) and npm (`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`) also work. Then run `claude --version` and `claude`. Docs are at code.claude.com/docs.

faq.question: Is Claude Code free?
faq.answer: The tool is free to install, but it is not included in the free claude.ai plan. You need Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise, a Console account, or a cloud provider such as Amazon Bedrock. As of October 2026 Pro is listed at $20 per month and Max starts at $100; see Claude's pricing page for current terms.

faq.question: Can I use Claude Code with HagiCode?
faq.answer: Yes. Install and sign in to Claude Code, then choose it as the Agent CLI in HagiCode. Claude Code is the agent that gets interactive questions and the agent work panel there.

faq.question: Does HagiCode replace Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. HagiCode runs Claude Code as its executor and adds sessions, proposals, commits and multi-repo tools around it. You can still run `claude` on the same repositories.

faq.question: Is this about the Claude model or Claude Code?
faq.answer: This page is about Claude Code, the coding agent. The Claude models behind it are billed through your Anthropic plan or provider, not through HagiCode.

faq.question: Claude Code vs HagiCode: which should I pick?
faq.answer: Pick Claude Code alone for terminal, editor, CI or single-task work. Add HagiCode when you want OpenSpec proposals, a unified view of many sessions, or multi-repo workspaces on top of Claude Code.
